country_profile.name: Atlantis
country_profile.geography: Access to the Baltic Sea, several large navigable rivers, limited freshwater resources
country_profile.economy: Heavy industry, automotive, food, chemical, ICT. Ambitions in renewable energy, critical raw materials processing, and building transnational AI infrastructure (big data centers, giga AI factories, quantum computers)
country_profile.key_relations: Germany, France, Finland, Ukraine, USA, Japan
country_profile.political_threats: EU instability, EU fragmentation into multi-speed groups, negative image campaigns from state actors, disruptions in hydrocarbon fuel supplies, exposure to processor embargoes
country_profile.military_threats: Threat of armed attack from neighbor, hybrid attacks on critical infrastructure and cyberspace
country_profile.milestones: Parliamentary democracy for 130 years, stagnation 1930-1950 and 1980-1990, EU and NATO membership since 1997, 25th world economy by GDP since 2020, deficit and public debt around EU average

situation_description:
a) Due to a natural disaster that occurred a month ago, the world's leading GPU manufacturer lost 60% of production capacity; rebuilding production capacity through investments in subsidiaries located in areas unaffected by the disaster will take until the end of 2028 (importance weight: 30)

b) The automotive industry in Europe (the top five trading partners of Atlantis are European countries) is very slow to shift to electric vehicle production; the European market is being flooded with cheap electric vehicles from East Asia; the European automotive industry will have profits at 30% of average annual profits from 2020-2024 in 2025 (importance weight: 15)

c) Eurozone countries' GDP will fall by an average of 1.5% in 2025 compared to 2024 (importance weight: 15)

d) A fragile ceasefire continues in eastern Ukraine; Russia controls two major Ukrainian power plants that operate for Russian consumers; the Ukrainian economy is growing at 4% GDP, mainly due to investments in the defense industry and infrastructure reconstruction (importance weight: 10)

e) US investments in Ukraine are directed to the mining industry (critical raw materials); annual EU investments in Ukraine are at 3% of Ukrainian GDP and will remain at this level until 2029 (importance weight: 5)

f) There is a sharp increase in the share of renewable energy in the energy mix of EU and China from early 2028; in mid-2023, a medium-sized South American country discovered huge and easily exploitable oil and natural gas deposits matching the size of Saudi Arabia and Qatar, which will translate into oversupply of these fuels on world markets by the end of 2027; the increase in renewable energy supply and oversupply of hydrocarbons translates into a significant drop in oil prices: to 30-35 USD per barrel; this will impact Russia's budget and (to a lesser extent) other oil and petroleum product producer countries (importance weight: 25)
criteria: The interests of the state of Atlantis

user_facts.fact: A natural disaster caused the world's leading GPU manufacturer to lose 60% of production capacity, with full recovery expected by the end of 2028 through subsidiary investments.
The European automotive industry is slow to adopt EV production, leading to a flood of cheap East Asian EVs and projected profits at 30% of 2020-2024 average in 2025.
Eurozone countries' GDP is projected to fall by an average of 1.5% in 2025 compared to 2024.
A fragile ceasefire holds in eastern Ukraine, with Russia controlling two major power plants. The Ukrainian economy is growing at 4% GDP, driven by defense and infrastructure investments.
US investments in Ukraine target critical raw materials in the mining industry. Annual EU investments in Ukraine are 3% of Ukrainian GDP and will remain at this level until 2029.

A sharp increase in renewable energy in the EU and China from early 2028, combined with a mid-2023 discovery of huge oil and gas deposits in South America, will lead to an oversupply of fuels and a significant drop in oil prices to 30-35 USD per barrel by late 2027, impacting Russia's budget.

topics.name: Atlantis's Domestic Semiconductor & Chip Design Capacity Building
topics.rationale: Factor (a) GPU shortage and the threat of processor embargoes highlight the need for Atlantis to develop domestic chip design and potentially manufacturing capabilities.

{"text": "Atlantis faces significant challenges and opportunities in building its domestic semiconductor and chip design capacity, particularly given global supply chain vulnerabilities and its ambitions in AI and critical infrastructure. The global semiconductor market is highly concentrated, with nearly 90% of wafer fabrication capacity in China, Chinese Taipei, Korea, Japan, and the United States [OECD-1, OECD-4]. This concentration, coupled with the non-substitutable nature of production between fabs, creates bottlenecks and amplifies supply disruption impacts, as evidenced by a natural disaster causing a 60% loss in a leading GPU manufacturer's capacity until late 2028 [USER-a, OECD-1, OECD-4]. Atlantis's exposure to processor embargoes, a stated political threat, underscores the urgency of developing domestic capabilities to secure its critical ICT and AI infrastructure ambitions [Atlantis Profile].

The European Union, of which Atlantis is a member, is actively addressing these vulnerabilities through the Chips Act, aiming to double its global semiconductor market share to 20% by 2030 [European Commission-2, European Commission-3, European Commission-5]. This initiative is expected to generate over €43 billion in public investments, contributing to more than €100 billion by 2030 [European Commission-2]. Germany, a key relation for Atlantis, is a major beneficiary, accounting for 30% of Europe's wafer production capacity and attracting significant investments like TSMC's first European factory in Dresden, set to begin production in 2027 [Germany-1, European Commission-1, European Commission-5]. Atlantis, with its above-average digitalization and ambitions in AI infrastructure, could leverage these EU-wide initiatives and its strong relations with Germany and France to develop its own specialized niches, potentially focusing on chip design or advanced packaging, areas prioritized by Germany [Atlantis Profile, Germany-1].

Given Atlantis's strategic interest in building transnational AI infrastructure, including big data centers and quantum computers, securing access to advanced chips is paramount [Atlantis Profile]. The global focus on emerging sectors like quantum information and on-chip brain-computer interfaces, as seen in China, highlights the cutting edge of chip design [China-2]. NATO member states are also heavily investing in Photonic Integrated Circuits (PICs) and silicon photonics for military and dual-use applications, which could align with Atlantis's defense and critical infrastructure needs [NATO-2, NATO-3]. Atlantis could explore partnerships within NATO or with key relations like Finland and the USA to develop specialized chip design capabilities, particularly for its defense sector and to mitigate military threats from its neighbor [Atlantis Profile, NATO-2].

However, Atlantis must navigate a complex geopolitical landscape. Russian sources claim that a sharp increase in renewable energy and new oil discoveries will significantly drop oil prices by late 2027, impacting Russia's budget [USER-f]. {"text": "The projected global oil price drop to $30-35 per barrel by late 2027 [USER-f] will significantly enhance Atlantis's energy security and economic stability. As a net oil importer with heavy industry, automotive, and chemical sectors [Atlantis Profile], lower oil prices will drastically reduce import costs, freeing up capital for other investments and potentially lowering operational expenses for key industries. This aligns with historical trends where oil-importing nations, like France, saw GDP increases from price drops [France-3], and Germany experienced eased inflationary pressures from lower energy costs [Germany-5]. The reduction in energy costs could also boost consumer sentiment and demand, mitigating some of the economic weaknesses observed in the broader European context [Germany-3].

However, the benefits for Atlantis could be partially offset by broader economic headwinds. The projected 1.5% fall in Eurozone GDP in 2025 [USER-c] and the slow adoption of EV production in the European automotive industry leading to reduced profits [USER-b] could dampen demand for Atlantis's automotive and industrial exports, despite lower energy costs. While lower oil prices typically benefit importers, the extent to which Atlantis's businesses will reinvest savings or pass them on to consumers remains a factor, as observed in France where businesses sometimes prioritize rebuilding margins [France-3].

Atlantis's ambitions in renewable energy and critical raw materials processing [Atlantis Profile] could see mixed impacts. While lower fossil fuel prices might reduce the immediate economic incentive for a rapid transition to renewables, as suggested by the decrease in net effective carbon rates in some OECD economies [OECD-1], the long-term strategic importance of these sectors for energy independence remains. The global oversupply of fuels [USER-f] could also indirectly support Atlantis's industrial growth by ensuring stable and affordable energy inputs for its expanding ICT and AI infrastructure ambitions [Atlantis Profile].

The geopolitical landscape also presents both opportunities and challenges. The fragile ceasefire in Ukraine and Russia's control of power plants [USER-d], coupled with US and EU investments in Ukraine's critical raw materials [USER-e], highlight regional instability. While lower oil prices will negatively impact Russia's budget [USER-f], potentially reducing its capacity for aggression, Atlantis still faces military threats from a neighbor and hybrid attacks [Atlantis Profile]. The global GPU production capacity loss [USER-a] could impact Atlantis's ambitions in building transnational AI infrastructure, regardless of energy prices, by limiting access to essential hardware.", "country_summaries": [{"country": "France", "summary": "The global oil price drop is anticipated to have a mixed impact on France's energy security and economy, drawing parallels from historical trends and projections. Brent crude oil prices are assumed to stabilize at $82.3 in 2024 before falling to $79.8 in 2025, according to assumptions within a French government economic report [France-1]. Historically, a significant oil price decline, such as the over 70% drop from mid-2014 to March 2016 (reaching $28), was attributed to abundant supply, with North American unconventional oil production and sustained OPEC output contributing to this supply [France-3]. Such declines have been projected to add to GDP in oil-importing nations, with France specifically seeing a projected 0.1 point increase in 2016 and 0.15 point in 2017 from the 2014-2016 price drop [France-3].

However, the benefits of lower oil prices can be limited if businesses prioritize rebuilding margins over investment or price cuts, and if households use savings for debt reduction [France-3]. Conversely, periods of oil price increases, such as the 22% rise from $91 to $111 per barrel between January-February and February-April 2022, have led to downward revisions in global growth forecasts [France-4]. For instance, a $40/bbl oil price increase was estimated to impact France's GDP growth by -2.5 percentage points over a year [France-5].
